evidence.title: Kidnapping convictions overturned in 3-year-old boy's tragic case

occurrences.checkable_against: U.S. 10th Circuit Court of Appeals mandate and district court docket
occurrences.quote_span: The court remanded that part of the case back to the district court, clearing the way for new trials for the men if prosecutors opt to pursue the case.
occurrences.speaker: U.S. 10th Circuit Court of Appeals
occurrences.subject: U.S. 10th Circuit Court of Appeals

occurrences.checkable_against: prosecution filings and 2023 trial record
occurrences.quote_span: Prosecutors alleged that it was under Leveille’s instruction that the family fled Georgia with the boy, ending up in a remote stretch of the high desert where they conducted firearms and tactical training to prepare for attacks against the government.
occurrences.speaker: prosecutors
occurrences.subject: U.S. 10th Circuit Court of Appeals

occurrences.checkable_against: 2023 trial transcript in the Taos compound case
occurrences.quote_span: During the three-week trial in 2023, the defendants suggested that the case was the product of “government overreach” and that they were targeted because they are Muslim.

occurrences.subject: U.S. 10th Circuit Court of Appeals

occurrences.checkable_against: U.S. 10th Circuit Court of Appeals judgment

figure.unit: possibility of retrial on kidnapping charges

occurrences.quote_span: The family members can’t be retried on the kidnapping charges, the panel ruled.

occurrences.subject: U.S. 10th Circuit Court of Appeals

occurrences.checkable_against: U.S. 10th Circuit Court of Appeals decision and trial jury instructions
occurrences.quote_span: The appellate panel took issue with jury instructions that implied the mother’s lack of consent could satisfy the unlawfulness element under the federal kidnapping statute.
occurrences.speaker: U.S. 10th Circuit Court of Appeals
occurrences.subject: U.S. 10th Circuit Court of Appeals

occurrences.checkable_against: U.S. 10th Circuit Court of Appeals judgment
occurrences.quote_span: The appeals panel also vacated convictions stemming from accusations that Wahhaj and his brother-in-law were preparing for attacks against the government.

occurrences.checkable_against: prosecution filings and 2023 trial record

occurrences.checkable_against: U.S. 10th Circuit Court of Appeals judgment in the Taos compound case
occurrences.quote_span: A federal appeals court has vacated kidnapping convictions in a case involving the death of a 3-year-old boy who went missing from Georgia in 2017 and later turned up dead at a squalid compound in New Mexico.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: U.S. 10th Circuit Court of Appeals

occurrences.checkable_against: 2018 trial testimony and forensic evidence in the Taos compound case

figure.unit: months stated for body retention duration

occurrences.quote_span: Testimony indicated that the boy died just weeks after arriving in New Mexico and that his body was kept for months with Leveille promising the others he would be resurrected.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: U.S. 10th Circuit Court of Appeals

occurrences.checkable_against: federal indictment, plea agreement, and sentencing judgment for Jany Leveille
occurrences.quote_span: A fifth defendant — Jany Leveille, a Haitian national — avoided the trial by pleading guilty to conspiracy to provide material support to terrorists and being in possession of a firearm while unlawfully in the United States. She was sentenced to 15 years in prison.

occurrences.checkable_against: 2018 law-enforcement raid inventory and reports for the Taos compound
occurrences.quote_span: Authorities raided the compound in 2018, finding 11 children and dismal living conditions. They also found 11 firearms and ammunition that were used at a makeshift shooting range on the property near the Colorado state line.

occurrences.subject: U.S. 10th Circuit Court of Appeals

occurrences.checkable_against: 2024 federal sentencing judgments in the Taos compound case
occurrences.quote_span: The boy’s father and other family members were sentenced to life in prison in 2024 after jurors convicted them in what prosecutors described as a “sick end-of-times scheme.”
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: U.S. 10th Circuit Court of Appeals

occurrences.checkable_against: U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of New Mexico email statement
occurrences.quote_span: “What happened at the Taos compound was horrific. We are reviewing the case and assessing what further action may be appropriate,” the U.S. attorney’s office for the district of New Mexico wrote in an email Wednesday.
occurrences.speaker: U.S. attorney’s office for the district of New Mexico
occurrences.subject: U.S. 10th Circuit Court of Appeals

occurrences.checkable_against: U.S. 10th Circuit Court of Appeals decision
occurrences.quote_span: “This instructional error was not harmless,” the panel wrote. “Had the court correctly instructed on the law, the jury couldn’t have found unlawfulness based on the government’s evidence.”

figure.unit: evidence of a federal kidnapping crime

occurrences.quote_span: A panel of the U.S. 10th Circuit Court of Appeals wrote in a decision issued Tuesday that there was no evidence of a federal kidnapping crime when the family took the boy, noting that no court order or state law made it illegal for Siraj Ibn Wahhaj to take his son.
